minutes.headline: Town Meeting rejected a cut to the school budget and voted on sewer, cable and cemetery articles; building-authority debate ran long.
minutes.summary: The captions open mid-debate on a motion to cut a school line, which was defeated. Meeting then took up stabilization fund transfers, sewer and solid waste enterprise budgets, water, cable access, cemetery, bond premium and borrowing articles, followed by a long presentation and floor debate on Articles 22 to 25 about the Ritter, Brooks House, old primary school and Town Hall buildings. The result of the building articles is not in the captions.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting defeated a motion to reduce a school budget line, after debate on special education hiring and a team psychologist.
The total budget under Article 8 passed.
Articles on stabilization funds, the OPEB trust and sewer reserves were put to votes, but the outcomes are not audible in the captions.
The cable access appropriation carried, and the article applying a bond premium to reduce turf field borrowing passed.
Debate on Articles 22 to 25, covering the Ritter, Brooks House, old primary school and Town Hall buildings, ran long; the outcome is not in the captions.

why_it_matters: The school line stayed intact, and the total budget passed, so the spending set here feeds into next year's tax bill.
The stabilization, OPEB and sewer reserve articles set money aside for future costs, and the captions do not show whether they passed.
The building articles could change who owns and uses town buildings, and residents raised concern about acting before the cost of a new municipal building is known.
